newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot LPGs steady in ever-quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot LPGs steady in ever-quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices were stable in extremely quiet trade late Tuesday as players stood on the sidelines to watch crude oil futures.
"People are jittery about crude," said a Midwest player referring to volatility on the futures market ahead of gasoline seasonal spring rally and cold weather.

In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane stayed steady at between 34.25 cents and 34.50 cents a gallon. Conway material held onto its quarter cent midday gain, trading at 34.50/34.75 cents.
Players said there was little fundamental news in the market except for an expected announcement next week on the supplier of Venezuela's tender for 60,000 tonnes of propane.
"That's about the only news in the market right now," said a Houston player. "No one really needs to do anything."
The ethane and butane markets were also steady and quiet in thin activity.

In other news, Texaco Inc. said Tuesday its Texaco Expanded NGL Distribution System will start full operations in early 1998. The 500-mile pipeline network was designed by Texaco to distribute NGLs to growing markets across South Louisiana.
The system will transport about 230,000 barrels of product daily and is expected to cost $70 million. ((--Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
